newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iran accuses U.S. of totalitarianism, terrorism.
newsitem.headline: Iran accuses U.S. of totalitarianism, terrorism.

text.p: Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati accused the United States on Monday of "totalitarianism at the international level" including "terrorist activities" and unilateral sanctions against Iran.
"The irreconcilability of totalitarianism with the rule of law has found dangerous manifestations in the international scene," he said in a speech to the General Assembly.

"The passing and signature of the (U.S.) legislation to allocate money for subversive and terrorist activities against the Islamic Republic of Iran is the most dangerous manifestation of this lawlessness."
Velayati asserted that the U.S. actions were no longer confined to the secrecy of intelligence services "but recklessly legislated into law by the United States Congress."

"This law and similar unlawful behavior, including the infamous decision of the U.S. Supreme Court approving kidnapping by the U.S. government, represent a very dangerous trend," he said, referring to U.S. legislation permitting the seizure of suspected terrorists abroad.

He said a similar pattern of U.S. behavior manifested in recent years was the "self-arrogation of the right to legislate for the international community by attempting to apply its domestic legislation beyond its borders" -- an allusion to laws aimed at deterring foreign investment in the oil industries of Iran and Libya, which Washington accuses of involement in terrorism.

Velayati said recent "unilateral sanctions enacted by the United States against trade partners of a number of countries" were a grave breach of international law and General Assembly resolutions. They were also a blatant interference in the affairs of other states and pointed to a dangerous trend that undermined the foundations of inter-state relations, he said.

He said the most notable manifestation of the "new international totalitarianism" was in the cultural sphere. While the world was characterized by diversity of religions, civilizations, cultures and customs, "the claimants of world leadership have either failed to grasp this self-evident reality due to their own lack of historical and cultural depth or have found it incompatible with their interests and thereby attempt to neglect it."

Speaking of a "misguided propaganda war waged to distort the image of Islam," Velayati declared: "The progressive march of the Islamic world, which benefits from the rich heritage of Islamic culture, history and civilization, cannot be halted, and thus this significant and important segment of humanity will certainly occupy an increasingly more prominent role in the shaping of the future world order."
In another reference to the United States, the Iranian minister said the Security Council had "repeatedly fallen prey to the interests of a permanent member."

Referring to Israel, he said: "Relying on such unconditional support, the Zionist regime continues with impunity its expansionist policies of occupation of Palestine, southern Lebanon and Syrian Golan coupled with its routine practice of state terrorism and blatant violation of the most fundamental rights of the Muslim people of Palestine."
